newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-TUFNELL STAKES CLAIM AS ENGLAND ROUT NZ XI.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TUFNELL STAKES CLAIM AS ENGLAND ROUT NZ XI.

text.p: Spinner Phil Tufnell staked a claim to a test place on Thursday as he bowled the visiting England side to a crushing innings win over a New Zealand Selection XI.
Tufnell captured five for 58 as the tourists swept to victory in the four-day match by an innings and 113 runs.
The Selection XI lost test batsman Adam Parore inside the first hour, caught by wicketkeeper Stewart off fast-medium Chris Silverwood for 13.
The home side's innings then fell apart in the hour before lunch as they lost three wickets in 22 balls.
Matt Horne was caught by Nick Knight at silly point off Tufnell, Mark Greatbatch was run out and Justin Vaughan taken at second slip by Knight off Silverwood.
Opener Blair Pocock had defied the England attack for over three hours for 43, but fell when he tried to sweep Tufnell and was caught by a diving Nasser Hussain at slip.

Danny Morrison, holder of the record number of ducks in tests, enjoyed himself by smashing 30 from 24 balls including a six over long-on off Tufnell. The bowler finally took his revenge by having him stumped.
"I was happy with the way I bowled," Tufnell said. "There was a little bit of turn and bounce."
Tufnell had grabbed 11 for 147 to bowl England to an innings win in the first test at Christchurch during their 1992 New Zealand tour.
Silverwood also enhanced his test prospects, collecting three for 29 from 14.1 overs.
The victory was set up by England batsmen Alec Stewart and Nasser Hussain, who both made centuries in the tourists' big first innings of 427 for eight declared.
"It went exactly to plan," England coach David Lloyd said. "We're here to win cricket matches and that's an ideal start."
New Zealand coach Steve Rixon was unimpressed with what he saw in the match.
"There were a number of players in that game who were on trial and it really hasn't helped the situation as far as selection goes," he said.
